newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open at record high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open at record high.

text.p: Australian shares climbed to a record high at the opening on Friday although activity remained as tight as in recent days.
The All Ordinaries index climbed 9.5 points to 2,600.1, surpassing Thursday's previous record high of 2,591.5.
The exercise of May series options after Thursday's expiry inflated volumes, with over A$993 million (US$762 million) in turnover put through prior to the market opening.
"It's very strong and it's been across the board," said dealer Richard Herring of Burrell and Co, citing the banks and buildings materials stocks as impressive early performers.

Sector leader National Australia Bank was strongest in its group, adding 20 cents to an intraday high of A$18.75. In building materials Boral stole the show, climbing over two percent to A$4.18. Chemicals group ICI Australia added 10 to A$12.21 after anouncing a A$360 million share buyback.
BHP was the miners' shining light, jumping 1.7 percent to A$18.92 although others made good gains, aided by position resetting after Thursday's May expiries.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about two to one, while about 39 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
